<abbr title="Koh-Lanta: The Sacred Fire">'''''Koh-Lanta: Le Feu Sacré'''''</abbr> is the twenty-ninth season of ''[[Koh-Lanta]]''. It was broadcast on TF1 from February 21 to June 13, 2023.

After 40 days, [[Frédéric Khouvilay]] defeated [[Tania Cakarevic]] in a 7-2 [[jury]] vote to become the [[Sole Survivor]].

==Production==
{{Empty section}}

==Twists/Changes==
* '''Sacred Fire Talisman:''' The winner of the first [[Reward Challenge]] earns the Sacred Fire Talisman which holds significant powers:
** If their [[tribe]] loses the [[Immunity Challenge]], the holder can use the Talisman as an [[Immunity Idol]] to protect themselves or a tribemate of their choice. The Talisman can only be used once the votes have already been cast.
** If their tribe wins the Immunity Challenge, the holder visits the losing tribe's [[camp]]. At [[Tribal Council/International|Tribal Council]], the holder of the Talisman has the ability to protect a castaway of their choice.
** At each [[Reward Challenge]], the Talisman comes back into play. If the owner's tribe wins Reward, the owner can keep the Talisman. If they lose, they have to give the Talisman to someone on the rival tribe.
** At the [[merge]], the holder is immune from the [[Ambassadors]] meeting, but can't become an Ambassador. They would also be immune at the first post-merge [[Tribal Council]].
*'''[[Tribe Leader|Tribe Captains]]:''' At the marooning, the castaways immediately compete in an individual Reward Challenge where both the first-placing man and the first-placing woman become the captains of the two new tribes. After spending the first night together, the tribes are then selected in a [[Schoolyard Pick]] right before the first Immunity Challenge, respecting gender parity.
* '''Secret Weapons:''' Like ''[[Koh-Lanta: Les Armes Secrètes|Les Armes Secrètes]]'', strategic weapons have been hidden on both sides with each of them having a different power.
** [[Vote Steal|Vote Diversion]]: Allows a castaway to steal another castaway's vote at Tribal Council.
** [[Extra Vote]]: Allows a castaway to vote twice at Tribal Council.
* '''[[Hidden Immunity Idol|Hidden Immunity Necklaces]]:''' Immunity Necklaces (the equivalent of Hidden Immunity Idols in ''Koh-Lanta'') are hidden at each of the two tribes' camps.
* '''Sudden Death Challenge:''' On Day 10, the castaway who comes in last in the Reward Challenge is directly eliminated from the game.
* '''Replacements After [[Quit]]s:''' For the first time since {{S2|12fr}}, quitters would be replaced even after the first cycle.
* '''Impromptu [[Tribal Council]]:''' In Episode 6, Tribal Council is held immediately after the [[Immunity Challenge]] at the challenge site. This also occurred immediately after the [[Reward Challenge]] at the challenge site in "Episode 13".
* '''Black Vote:''' The Black Vote keeps the mechanics introduced in {{S2|20fr}}. Starting from the first post-merge Tribal Council, the person voted out gives a remaining castaway the power to vote twice at the following Tribal Council.
* '''{{Dab-twist|Tied Destinies}}:''' On Day 30, the eight remaining castaways were divided into four pairs by a rock draw. Until the next Tribal Council, the fate of each castaway is linked to their partner: the challenges are competed as pairs, and the castaway voted out at Tribal Council also causes their partner's elimination.
* '''Re-entry [[Duel]]:''' After the [[Tied Destinies (twist)|Tied Destinies]] twist, the two eliminated castaways competed in a [[Redemption Island (twist)/International|duel to return to the game]]. The winner would then compete in a second duel against the castaway who was voted out at the following Impromptu Tribal Council. The losers of each duel would be permanently eliminated.
* '''[[Final Tribal Council]]:''' The standard [[Final Two|two-finalist]] Final Tribal Council returns after the previous season featured a [[Final Three|three-finalist]] finale.
